references.text: God promises to raise up a prophet who will speak His words, just as Jesus emphasizes that His teaching is not His own but from the One who sent Him.
Moses points out that one must not add to or take away from God's words, which underscores Jesus' claim that His teaching is a pure transmission from the Father.
God promises to put His words in the prophet's mouth, a direct parallel to Jesus' assertion that His teaching comes from the One who sent Him.
The Lord says to Jeremiah: 'I have put My words in your mouth,' which reflects Jesus' authority as one who speaks God's words and not his own.
Jesus later confirms that His message is God's message, and that He does not speak on His own but as the Father has commanded Him.
Jesus says that He does nothing on His own but speaks as the Father has taught Him, which is a direct extension of the theme in 7:16.
